title: Versioned generic worker profiles, resource requests and scheduling contract
body:
## Objective
Extend existing #112 capability advertisement and #198 admission, not replace them. Profiles are reusable policy/requirement overlays, independent of machine brands and test frameworks.
## Work
- [ ] Audit #49/#50/#112 capability schema, existing Cezar worker metadata and #198. Define typed versioned inventory (OS/architecture, executors, installed runtimes, resource quantities, isolation, display, network, storage/accessibility, custom namespaced capabilities) and freshness semantics.
- [ ] Define portable requested requirements: hard capabilities, min resources, affinity/anti-affinity, exclusive/shared leases, max concurrency, network isolation zone, scheduling priority, profile tags, locality preference; use deterministic boolean matching with explainable reasons.
- [ ] Profiles are declarative templates and policy defaults (e.g. general-compute, gui, lightweight-network-peer, asset-enabled); admin may attach multiple profiles/overrides; reject unsafe narrowing/privilege escalation and stale inventory.
- [ ] Bind worker selection to #198 atomic admission, contention/fairness/backpressure; distinguish resources reserved for coding vs verification without second queue.
- [ ] Schema migrations, defaults for pre-existing local-only workers, version negotiation, redacted inspection CLI and fixtures for Windows/Linux/other OS compatibility.
## Acceptance
- [ ] Identical test requests match different hardware with equivalent advertised capabilities; changing resource inventory changes matching without source code modification.
- [ ] Unschedulable, stale, incompatible, saturated, and policy-denied are distinct reason codes. Same-display exclusive jobs serialize. No double allocation under concurrency.
- [ ] Existing local-only worker configuration and current test adapters still work.
## Depends on
#49 #50 #112 #198; coordinate transport child #214 (verify actual issue ID if ordering differs).

## Cross-cutting constraints
- Parent #213; reuse #47 #49 #50 #112 #113 #198; generic core with project-owned adapters. No hardcoded host hardware, OS-specific paths, Godot-only schema or duplicate scheduler/store.
- Preserve single-node/backward compatibility and no GitHub Actions compute. Negative/failure tests, docs, schema versioning, audited local rollout, reviewed PR and evidence required.
